question.worked_solution:
First, recall that

$$
{lim}_{t\to 2}f(t)=⟨{lim}_{t\to 2}{e}^{t-2},\,{lim}_{t\to 2}\sqrt{6-t},\,{lim}_{t\to 2}\frac{3}{t+2}⟩.
$$

Now, we find the limits one by one.

- For the first component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 2}{e}^{t-2} & ={e}^{2-2} \\  & ={e}^{0} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 2}\sqrt{6-t} & =\sqrt{6-2} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the third component, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 2}\frac{3}{t+2} & =\frac{3}{2+2} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{t\to 2}f(t)=⟨1,2,\frac{3}{4}⟩.$
